Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has expressed gratitude to Yobe State Governor and the people of Potiskum for what he described as a peaceful and welcoming reception during the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Affordable Life campaign rally in the state.
Atiku also took a swipe at President Bola Tinubu over allegations of using artificial intelligence (AI) to inflate the crowd figures at presidential campaign events, insisting that the massive turnout witnessed in Potiskum was genuine and required no digital enhancement.
In a statement issued on Monday by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reception he received from the moment his campaign team arrived in Potiskum from Azare, Bauchi State, was a testament to the people’s desire for a better and more affordable Nigeria.
He described the crowd, enthusiasm and warm reception as overwhelming, expressing appreciation to residents of Potiskum and the wider Yobe State for embracing the ADC’s campaign message.
“The welcome from the moment we entered Potiskum from Azare was simply breathtaking. The sea of heads, the joyful faces, the chants and the warmth of the people will remain in my heart.
“To the people of Potiskum and to the good people of Yobe State, I say thank you. You opened your doors and your hearts to us, and we are deeply grateful,” he said.
The former vice president also commended the Yobe State Governor for providing what he described as a level playing field, allowing the ADC campaign to proceed without rancour or unnecessary obstruction.
According to him, democracy thrives when political parties are allowed to freely engage voters and communicate their policies and programmes without interference.
“I also thank the Governor of Yobe State for ensuring that our campaign could proceed on a level playing field. Democracy is strengthened when every party can meet the people freely and present its message. We appreciate the opportunity to bring our vision to Yobe,” Atiku stated.
Taking a swipe at the Presidency over the alleged use of AI-generated images to enhance campaign crowd figures, Atiku maintained that the turnout in Potiskum was made up of real people whose presence could not be manufactured.
“The Presidency may need artificial intelligence to conjure a crowd, but in Potiskum the people came out in flesh and blood, unfiltered, unedited and impossible to fabricate. Our Affordable Life campaign needs no artificial crowd; the people’s presence and their voices speak for themselves,” he said.
He further mocked the alleged AI-generated crowd images, suggesting that the technology appeared to have overlooked basic realities about how people attend political rallies.
“The Presidency’s AI must have forgotten that crowds need seats and that people do not fly. Perhaps in Tinubu’s imaginary rally, the supporters were expected to hover through the speech,” he added.
Atiku also used the opportunity to reaffirm his commitment to the ADC’s Affordable Life campaign, saying the enthusiasm of supporters and chants calling for political change reflected growing public dissatisfaction with the current administration.
He said the repeated chant of “Tinubu Must Go” at ADC rallies was more than a political slogan, describing it as a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility awaiting whoever receives the people’s mandate.
“When I hear the crowd chanting ‘Tinubu Must Go’ at our rallies, I take those words personally. They are a call for change and a reminder of the responsibility that will come with the people’s mandate,” he said.
Atiku further pledged that, if elected president in the January 16 presidential election, he would take immediate steps to address the rising cost of living and restore affordability to the lives of Nigerians.
He expressed confidence that good governance and economic relief would follow the end of Tinubu’s administration on May 29, 2027.
“The ADC’s Affordable Life campaign is not mere sloganeering. When President Tinubu leaves office on 29 May 2027, good governance and an affordable life must follow.
“I solemnly pledge to take immediate steps to make life affordable again when elected president at the January 16 presidential election. That is my promise to our teeming supporters,” he declared.
The former vice president said the reception in Yobe had further strengthened his campaign’s resolve, adding that Nigerians would continue to respond positively to messages addressing their economic struggles and aspirations.
“Yobe has reminded us that when a message speaks to people’s struggles and aspirations, they will come out in their numbers to be heard,” he said.
